$comment: Book type catalogue (D-017). Every new book picks one type; the type names its structure template (config/book-templates/), starting word and unit ranges, genre rules, and the default interior theme (config/interior-themes.json) and cover style (config/cover-styles.json). Word and unit ranges are starting points for the owner to change per book, not market data. A field of health marks a health or care type: other non-fiction types get a field drift warning when their text mentions health institutions (owner, 21 October 2026). KDP facts are never copied here: kdpNotes point at rule ids in config/kdp-rules/. Trim sizes come from paperback.trimSizes.list, which is unverified until checked against KDP.

categories.name: Fiction
categories.description: Novels, novellas and story collections, written scene by scene with a story bible.

categories.name: Children's
categories.description: Picture books, bedtime stories and books for young readers, checked against the gentle content rules.

categories.name: Non-fiction
categories.description: First-person guides and narrative non-fiction with chapters, subheadings and key takeaways.

categories.name: Workbooks and journals
categories.description: Books the reader writes in, and poetry.

types.name: Contemporary romance
types.description: A love story set now, with a guaranteed happy or hopeful ending. Often the first of a series set in one town.

expectations: Two leads with alternating or close-third point of view
The relationship is the main plot
A happy ever after or happy for now ending
mustHaves: Meet moment in the first three chapters
A real obstacle that comes from character, not coincidence
A dark moment before the resolution
Heat level stated in the blueprint (sweet, clean, or warm with the door closed)
avoid: Explicit content unless the owner sets the heat level

kdpNotes.text: Series name and number go in the listing, not the title field.
Spine text only from 80 pages.

types.name: Historical romance
types.description: A love story set in a real past period, from Regency to the 1950s, with period detail kept accurate.

expectations: Period manners, dress and speech without modern slang
Social rules of the time create the obstacle
mustHaves: Story bible period sheet: year, place, class, money, travel
Historical note in the back matter separating fact from invention
Real historical people only in passing and never given invented private acts
avoid: Anachronistic words and attitudes presented as period-true
Invented historical facts presented as real

kdpNotes.text: Historical facts used as claims go to the claims-to-verify report.

types.name: Romantasy
types.description: Romance and fantasy with equal weight: a magic system, a world at stake and a central love story.

expectations: World rules set in the story bible and never broken
Romance arc and quest arc that turn on each other
Series hooks allowed but the romance resolves or clearly continues
mustHaves: Magic system with costs
Named places and a glossary
Point of view plan per chapter
avoid: Explicit content unless the owner sets it
Names or worlds lifted from existing series

kdpNotes.text: A map counts as an image: supply it at print resolution or leave it out.

types.name: Fantasy
types.description: Epic or quest fantasy in an invented world with its own history, magic and stakes.

expectations: A world that feels lived in
A quest or conflict with clear stakes
mustHaves: Story bible with history, factions, magic rules and a timeline
Glossary for invented words
Consistent naming
avoid: Info dumps in the first chapter
Borrowed names, places or magic from existing series

kdpNotes.text: Long books: check the page maximum for the trim before export.

types.name: Science fiction
types.description: Stories built on a scientific or technological idea: near future, space, or alternate worlds.

expectations: One central 'what if' explored with care
mustHaves: Story bible tech sheet: what exists, what it costs, what it cannot do
Timeline
avoid: Real science stated wrongly as fact

types.name: Thriller
types.description: High-stakes, fast-paced fiction with a ticking clock and a protagonist under threat.

expectations: Short chapters ending on a turn
A clear threat and a deadline
mustHaves: Twist plan in the blueprint: what the reader believes, what is true, when it flips
Clue ledger so every twist is fair
Antagonist plan with motive
avoid: Step-by-step instructions for real crimes or weapons
Gratuitous violence against children or animals

kdpNotes.text: Real crime methods presented as instructions are blocked by the claims check.

types.name: Mystery and crime
types.description: A crime, an investigator and a fair-play solution: police procedural, private detective or amateur sleuth.

expectations: Suspects with motive, means and opportunity
The solution uses clues the reader saw
mustHaves: Clue ledger: where each clue and red herring appears
Suspect sheet
Investigation timeline
avoid: Real police procedure stated wrongly as fact

types.name: Cosy mystery
types.description: A gentle whodunnit: an amateur sleuth, a close community, no gore and a satisfying reveal.

expectations: Amateur sleuth with a hobby or trade
mustHaves: Clue ledger and fair-play solution
Recurring cast for a series
Warm, witty tone

types.name: Horror (mild)
types.description: Atmospheric, unsettling fiction: ghost stories and quiet dread rather than gore.

mustHaves: Content notes in the front matter
Rules for the supernatural in the story bible
avoid: Harm to children on the page

kdpNotes.text: Content notes help readers; KDP content rules still apply.

types.name: Historical fiction
types.description: A story set in a real period, with invented characters living through real events.

mustHaves: Historical note separating fact from invention
Research sources for every period fact

kdpNotes.text: Period facts presented as true go to the claims-to-verify report.

types.name: Literary fiction
types.description: Character-led fiction where language, theme and inner life carry the story.

mustHaves: Voice sample approved before writing
Theme notes in the story bible
avoid: Purple prose and stock phrases (house style)
Epigraphs from quotes the owner did not supply

types.name: Short story collection
types.description: Several complete stories under one title, linked by theme, place or character.

expectations: A thread that ties the collection
mustHaves: Running order that varies length and mood
Story titles in title case
avoid: Stories that need the reader to have read another to make sense

types.name: Young adult
types.description: Fiction for readers aged 13 to 18 with a teenage protagonist and coming-of-age stakes.

expectations: Teen protagonist, first person or close third
mustHaves: Age-appropriate content notes
Helplines or resources only from research sources if a hard topic appears
avoid: Glamorised self-harm, drugs or risky behaviour

kdpNotes.text: Set the reading age honestly in the listing.

types.name: Picture book
types.description: A short illustrated story told across spreads, read aloud to children aged 3 to 7.

mustHaves: One new word used at least three times and explained
Scene prompt for every spread with the same character sheet
Happy, soothing ending

kdpNotes.text: Full-colour interior with bleed.
At least 24 pages; no spine text under 80 pages.

types.name: Bedtime story
types.description: A calm, soothing story for the last minutes of the day, with soft sounds, warm light and a goodnight line.

expectations: Sensory comfort: soft textures, quiet sounds, warm light
Repeated lines children can join in with
mustHaves: One new word per book, explained in child-friendly words
Goodnight message switched on
Both safety checks pass
avoid: Excitement that winds a child up at the end

kdpNotes.text: Full-colour interior with bleed.

types.name: Early reader
types.description: A first chapter-style book for children starting to read alone, with short sentences and simple words.

expectations: Short sentences and repeated sight words
mustHaves: New words list at the back
Large, clear type

kdpNotes.text: Colour interior; check printing cost before setting the price.

types.name: Chapter book
types.description: Short illustrated chapters for confident young readers, often a series with the same friends.

mustHaves: Chapters of 800 to 1,500 words
Simple vocabulary with a few stretch words
avoid: Adults solving the problem for the child

types.name: Middle grade
types.description: Novels for readers aged 8 to 12: adventure, friendship and a hero their age.

mustHaves: Age-appropriate stakes
Clear chapter endings that pull the reader on

types.name: Activity book
types.description: Puzzles, colouring, mazes, drawing prompts and word games for children.

expectations: Clear instructions a child can follow
mustHaves: Age range on the cover and in the listing
Thick, simple line art for colouring
avoid: Small parts or unsafe craft steps

kdpNotes.text: Activity and colouring books may count as low-content; ISBN rules differ.
Large trim: printing cost uses the large-trim table.

types.name: Self-help and personal growth
types.description: A first-person guide to changing a habit, a mindset or a part of life, with stories and steps.

expectations: Stories that show, then steps that help
mustHaves: Three or more subheadings per chapter
Key takeaways
Illustrative stories marked as such
avoid: Therapy or medical advice presented as fact

types.name: Business and money
types.description: Practical guides to starting, running or growing a small business or side income, with honest expectations.

expectations: Clear steps the reader can try this week
UK context: HMRC, VAT, sole trader basics pointed to official sources
mustHaves: Earnings disclaimer in the front matter
Resources only from research sources
avoid: Tax or legal advice presented as definitive
Invented case studies presented as real

kdpNotes.text: Money and tax statements go to the claims-to-verify report.

types.name: AI and technology how-to
types.description: Plain-English guides to using AI tools and everyday technology, written for beginners.

expectations: Step-by-step tasks with what the reader should see
Dated: tools change, so screens and prices carry the month checked
mustHaves: Practical variant with short lists
A safety and privacy note before any tool that handles personal data
Name only tools that appear in the research sources
avoid: Screenshots of third-party products without permission
Prices or features stated without a date

kdpNotes.text: Books mostly from public-domain or freely available content can be refused; write original text.

types.name: Health and wellbeing
types.description: Everyday wellbeing for general readers: sleep, food, movement and rest, without medical claims.

mustHaves: Medical disclaimer in the front matter
Every health statement in the claims-to-verify report
Point readers to their GP or NHS 111 for symptoms
avoid: Supplement or diet claims without sources

kdpNotes.text: Health claims are checked before export; unverified claims block the pack.

types.name: Healthcare professional
types.description: Books for nurses and other NHS staff on practice, leadership, education and wellbeing at work.

expectations: Reflective prompts a nurse can use on shift
mustHaves: Professional disclaimer: local policy and the NMC Code come first
NHS terms explained on first use
Clinical statements in the claims-to-verify report
Illustrative patient stories, never identifiable
Times on the 24-hour clock (03:40, 19:30)
Characters named by role (the nurse in charge, a healthcare assistant), with at most a passing surname such as Mr Khan
The exact words to say, in curly quotes, at least twice in each section
avoid: Invented guidance, policy numbers or statistics
Named composite characters with first names and backstories
Bulleted lists, boxes and headings below section level in the chapters

kdpNotes.text: Clinical and safety statements go to the claims-to-verify report before export.

types.name: Clinical reference guide
types.description: Quick-look reference handbooks for UK nurses and other NHS staff, such as an abbreviations guide, written as clean tables with no clinical instructions.

expectations: Easy to scan on shift: short orientation, then tables
Only terms in widespread UK NHS, NMC, RCN and Academy of Medical Royal Colleges use
Ambiguous or 'do not use' items flagged in a Take care note
mustHaves: Professional disclaimer: follow your employer's approved abbreviation list and local policy; the NMC Code comes first
Reference entries in Markdown tables, alphabetical inside each chapter
Ambiguous or do-not-use abbreviations flagged (for example U for units, QD, trailing zeros, MS versus MSO4 or MgSO4)
No doses, thresholds or treatment instructions anywhere
Clinical statements in the claims-to-verify report
avoid: Invented guidance, policy numbers or statistics

kdpNotes.text: Clinical and safety statements go to the claims-to-verify report before export.

types.name: Memoir and biography
types.description: A true life story told in scenes: the author's own, or a family member's with their consent.

mustHaves: Author note on names changed and memory
Narrative variant with no takeaways
Owner reviews every real person mentioned
avoid: Private details of living people without consent

types.name: Cookbook
types.description: Recipes grouped by meal or season, with method steps, timings and the cook's notes.

mustHaves: Serves, prep time and cook time on every recipe
Allergen note where common allergens appear
Food safety statements in the claims report
avoid: Recipes copied from other books or sites
Undercooking advice for meat, eggs or rice

kdpNotes.text: Colour photos raise printing cost a lot; check before choosing colour.

types.name: Travel
types.description: Guides and travel writing: where to go, how to get there and what it is like.

mustHaves: Prices, opening times and transport details marked with the month checked
Sources for every practical fact
avoid: Safety advice without an official source

types.name: Home, garden and hobbies
types.description: Practical guides to growing, making and fixing things at home, with clear steps and seasonal notes.

expectations: Steps the reader can follow at home
Honest about what can go wrong
mustHaves: Practical variant with short lists
Safety notes for tools, chemicals and plants that can harm pets or children
Seasonal timings checked against research sources
avoid: Health claims for plants or remedies

kdpNotes.text: Plant safety and remedy statements go to the claims-to-verify report.

types.name: Faith and spirituality
types.description: Devotional and reflective books: faith in everyday life, prayer, scripture and hope.

expectations: Scripture quoted accurately with the translation named
mustHaves: Bible translation chosen in the blueprint and its permission notice on the copyright page
Quotes checked word for word

kdpNotes.text: Scripture quotations need the translation's permission notice; the owner confirms it.

types.name: Parenting and family
types.description: Warm, practical help for parents and carers, from babies to teenagers.

mustHaves: Child health and safety statements in the claims report
Point to the GP, health visitor or NHS 111 for health worries

types.name: Education and study guide
types.description: Revision guides and study skills for students and adult learners, with worked examples.

mustHaves: Answers at the back
Exam board or syllabus named only if the owner confirms it

kdpNotes.text: Fill-in pages may change the VAT rate on print.

types.name: Workbook
types.description: A guide the reader works through: short teaching, then exercises, checklists and trackers.

expectations: Two to four exercises per chapter
mustHaves: Ruled lines sized for handwriting
Exercise types varied
avoid: Medical, legal or financial instructions in exercises

kdpNotes.text: Fill-in pages may change the VAT rate on print.

types.name: Guided journal
types.description: Prompts and space to write: gratitude, reflection, prayer or recovery, one entry a day.

expectations: Varied prompts that build over time
mustHaves: Writing lines sized for handwriting
Short intro on how to use it
avoid: Prompts that push readers into distress without signposting help

kdpNotes.text: Journals and planners are low-content books on KDP; ISBN handling differs.
Fill-in pages may change the VAT rate on print.

types.name: Planner
types.description: Undated or dated planning pages: weekly spreads, habit trackers, goals and notes.

expectations: Clear grid and generous writing space
mustHaves: Dated planners: dates checked by code, never by AI
Week starts on Monday for en-GB
avoid: Thin lines that do not print

kdpNotes.text: Low-content book; ISBN handling differs.

types.name: Poetry
types.description: A collection of poems grouped in sections, set with care for line breaks and white space.

expectations: A voice and theme across the collection
Each poem starts on a new page
mustHaves: Line breaks kept exactly in every format
Owner approves every poem

kdpNotes.text: Ebook line breaks need a reflowable layout check before upload.
